title: Attention routing oscillation: detection, quarantine, and mitigation playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description: During a capacity burst on Feb 7 we observed repeated oscillation of execution-path selection for models using the new attention microkernel (attn-fused-v2). Worker nodes alternated between the fused kernel and a dequantized fallback within 10–60s windows, causing repeated p95/p99 latency spikes and batch-thinning that impacted throughput for multi-tenant workloads. This ticket captures detection heuristics, short-term mitigations applied, and a playbook for preventing recurrence via scheduler and telemetry changes.
incident_summary: Regression manifested as ~2-3x p99 latency spikes during high concurrency. Root signals: kernel-assignment flip-rate, KV cache miss increase, average batch-size drop. A probe routine that samples alternate kernels amplified a temporary latency perturbation into sustained oscillation on several GPU pools.
reproduction_steps: Deploy model: open/attn-fused-v2:2026-01-30 with quantized weights on a 4-GPU pool
Generate concurrent traffic: 250 qps steady with 10% burst events that send 2x requests for 30s every 5 minutes
Run benchmark harness with kernel-probing enabled and a probe_interval=10s
Observe scheduler logs for kernel_choice changing back-and-forth and p95 latency increasing >200ms over baseline
telemetry_findings: Kernel flip-rate (choices per minute) correlated strongly with p95 latency spikes (Pearson r=0.78)
KV cache hit-rate dropped 18% when oscillation started, indicating warmed caches were being evicted by recompiled paths
Batch size median fell from 6->3 during oscillation windows, increasing unit cost
Probe tasks were queued with higher priority, causing recompile/priming work to preempt steady inference microbatches
root_cause_hypothesis: The scheduler's transient-latency-sensitive scoring plus an aggressive probe routine created positive feedback: small latency perturbations triggered kernel swap, causing cache and microbatch disruption that made the fallback look better, which then triggered another swap. Lack of hysteresis and insufficient prioritization separation between probes and production traffic allowed the oscillation to self-amplify.
temporary_mitigations: Rolled back probe window for attn-fused-v2 to disabled across affected pools (hotfix: deploy rollback PR #8473)
Applied a 30s cooldown/hysteresis in the scheduler for kernel changes (config toggle runtime.kernel_hysteresis=30s)
Lowered probe task priority so they cannot preempt production microbatches
Pinned the problematic model revision to the stable kernel scoring profile in Dedicated pools
long_term_actions: Add an Oscillation Index metric (kernel_flip_rate normalized by batch_size) and alert when >0.15 for 60s
Implement per-model quarantine: if flip_rate > threshold for 2 consecutive windows, force stable kernel and prevent probes for 10m
Refactor probe scheduler: separate lane with resource caps and exponential backoff when probes cause measurable latency regressions
Introduce kernel-change hysteresis into scoring algorithm (decay factor + minimum dwell time), with experimental flag to A/B test
Automated end-to-end benchmark: synthetic workload that reproduces oscillation patterns to validate fixes before rollout
Update rollout playbook to require canary traffic with observability gating for kernel stability metrics

acceptance_criteria: Oscillation Index metric exists in dashboards and fires alerts in a test scenario
Kernel-change hysteresis deployed behind feature flag and validated on canary pool without increasing baseline latency
Probe tasks cannot preempt production microbatches in overloaded pools (verified with load tests)
Synthetic benchmark reproduces prior oscillatory behavior and shows reduced flip-rate after fixes
notes: Decision: prefer conservative hysteresis + quarantine over aggressive probe elimination to avoid missing real regressions
Trade-off: quarantine increases mean latency for short windows for affected model versions but reduces systemic oscillation risk
Review feedback from SRE: require an automated rollback when Oscillation Index alert fires twice within 10 minutes
PM approval obtained for canary rollout plan on 2026-03-02
Follow-up: coordinate with model-onboarding to add 'sensitivity-to-probing' label so scheduler can apply different defaults
